chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Becoming a Master Mason in Boston with Sabby Lewis
summary: With Sabby Lewis he studied under a pool-hall teacher, joined Crispus Attucks Lodge, later the Beacon Light lodge in New York, and sponsored Budd Johnson.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: There's one other thing that I wanted to mention that requires going back a bit, I think. You mentioned, just yesterday I think it was, having belonged to the Masons at one time.
Well, at the time, I was... that was something new for me and I was with Sabby. I'll never forget Sabby and I became Master Masons in Boston. We studied, ohh my God we studied. I'll

never forget, this guy had a pool hall and he was our teacher. His name was Person, he played some guitar, years before that, and I'd go by the pool hall and study and I'd study at home and that's how I became a master Mason. Sabby Lewis and I went in together.
What first got your interest in that? Did you have a friend who was a Mason?

No. You know how you hear things, you know, that if you're a Mason it's good fellowship and you meet some fine men, you know what I mean, upstanding men. I didn't understand all of it but it attracted me because of the ritual and etcetera, etcetera. And it would help you...when you're a musician out on the road, because you're meeting all different kinds of people all the time. And it's good for your public relations. In other words, it would just show me a different facet of life, you know, that attracted me. So I became a master Mason in Boston, and then when I came to New York to stay I was admitted. It was the Crispus Attucks Lodge in Boston and
then when I came to New York I was admitted to the Beacon Light and I was instrumental in getting Budd Johnson. I was there the night Budd Johnson was made a master Mason. Yeah.
So how long did you remain active as a Mason?

Well, I remained active until I started goin' on the road. You know, I'd go to the meetings...and you know in Masonry you meet so many different people from so many different walks of life. It's a good fellowship.
So, in the lodge, were there very many musicians, or relatively few?

Well, only one I know in New York was...that I knew of at that time, was Budd, because, you know, I told him about it and he says, 'All right, I'll go on up there for your lodge,' and I was there and...the point I'm tryin' to bring out is there's a lot of musicians in New York who were Masons but they didn't go through the time I was...you see what I mean...and most of your musicians at the time..like one time I understand Basie's
whole band became (Masons)...you know, it was the thing to do. Yeah. Sure.
So what years was that? It would have been one of the Boston years so it would have been forty...
